children: Qatar's Lesha Bank has signed an MoU with Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), part of BlackRock, to invest more than $1 billion alongside the global infrastructure investor.

Under the MoU, Lesha Bank, a Shariah-compliant investment bank, and GIP will explore joint infrastructure investments, with a focus on GCC development opportunities and the region's economic transformation.

The agreement comes within days of Qatar disclosing plans to set up a dedicated platform, Doha Investment, to expand its wealth fund’s domestic portfolio. Also this week, the QIA and JPMorgan Chase & Co. agreed to set up a $20 billion partnership that leverages capabilities across public and private markets in both equities and credit.

BlackRock completed its acquisition of GIP earlier this year, creating one of the world's largest infrastructure investment platforms with significant exposure to energy, transport, digital and water assets.
(Writing by Brinda Darasha; editing by Daniel Luiz)

title: Qatar’s Lesha Bank eyes over $1bln in infrastructure with BlackRock GIP
